title: Right adjoint to proper étale derived direct image with finite coefficients
statement: Let X and Y be schemes and g : X → Y a proper morphism. Let Λ be a finite commutative ring. On the ordinary unbounded derived categories of étale sheaves of Λ-modules of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the total right derived functor Rg_* of the sheaf direct image admits a right adjoint. Neither X nor Y is assumed Noetherian or quasi-compact.

source.place: docstring of isLeftAdjoint_rightDerivedLowerShriek, proper factor; Stacks Project Tag 0F5Y, injectives-proposition-brown

proof.text: Work on a quasi-compact affine open of Y. Properness makes its inverse image quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Finite type gives a finite bound e for geometric fibre dimensions. Proper base change and the torsion cohomological-dimension theorem give R^q g_* F = 0 for q > 2e. The geometric fibres are quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so their cohomology commutes with filtered colimits. The stalk formula and conservative geometric stalks imply that all higher direct images commute with filtered colimits and hence with coproducts.

Apply the finite-amplitude unbounded coproduct argument on each affine open. The restriction of derived direct image to such an open is the derived direct image of the restricted proper map: restriction to an open is exact and preserves injectives, because it has an exact extension-by-zero left adjoint. Thus the global coproduct comparison restricts to an isomorphism on every affine open. Restriction detects isomorphisms of cohomology sheaves, and therefore of derived objects; hence Rg_* preserves coproducts globally. This argument needs only local finite amplitude, not a uniform global fibre-dimension bound.

The source is the unbounded derived category of a Grothendieck abelian category of étale module sheaves. Apply Stacks Project Tag 0F5Y, injectives-proposition-brown, to the exact coproduct-preserving Rg_*. Objectwise representability of Hom(Rg_*(-), K), followed by Yoneda, gives its right adjoint. This is the remaining Brown-representability part of the proper-factor argument.
